A small example NestedScale

Source: R/scale-construct.R
scale_example.Rd

A synthetic 3-frame hierarchy used in examples and tests. It deliberately reproduces three awkward features of real classification tables:

Usage

scale_example()

Value

A NestedScale with 7 leaves and frames sector/class/group/item.

Details

  • a code ("G1") reused at more than one frame, so bare codes are ambiguous and every lookup must name its frame;

  • a non-nesting pair of frames – group "GB" draws members from two different classes, so class and group do not form a tree;

  • a member ("OTH") with no code at any coarser frame (partial coverage).

Examples

s <- scale_example()
s
#> NestedScale: example
#> Description: Synthetic example: reused code, non-nesting frame pair, and an unassigned leaf 
#> Frames (4, coarsest first):
#>   - sector (2)  [1 member unassigned]
#>     - class (3)  [1 member unassigned]
#>       - group (3)  [1 member unassigned]
#>         - item (7)
#> Leaves: 7
#> Weights: size, count (default: size)
scale_nests(s, "class", "group") # FALSE - they cross-cut
#> [1] FALSE
#> attr(,"offenders")
#> [1] "GB"
